title: HB2710 (2020 Regular): RELATING TO PROTECTIVE ORDERS.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Hawaii) (gun-policy Stage 5, Hawaii); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Hawaii text (Introduced, official copy, https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2020/bills/HB2710_.HTM; sha256 7cda153d0eaf3c98f3d330a767c78cc4700313a3b90def0c6c15cb54b3e40043)
provenance.note: As filed. The firearm-search paragraphs are the bill's additions per its Description; the rest of each section is existing sentencing law restated. Section 2 repeats the seized-firearm sentence of Section 1 and Section 3 repeats it too; only the first is quoted for those parts.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (HRS 586-4(e)): A law enforcement officer, as defined in section 710-1000, shall be permitted to search a person convicted under this section, including the person's motor vehicle and the person's residence, for firearms without obtaining a search warrant pursuant to chapter 803 if the law enforcement officer has reason to believe acts of abuse or malicious property damage by the person are imminent. A firearm seized as a result of the search shall not be considered in any subsequent conviction if the court finds there was not probable cause for the search; provided that the firearm may be maintained by law enforcement until the registered owner of the firearm provides sufficient proof to law enforcement that the firearm will be properly stored.
SECTION 2 (HRS 586-11(a)): A law enforcement officer, as defined in section 710-1000, shall be permitted to search a person convicted under this section, including the person's motor vehicle and the person's residence, for firearms without obtaining a search warrant pursuant to chapter 803 if the law enforcement officer has reason to believe acts of abuse or malicious property damage by the person are imminent.
SECTION 3 (HRS 604-10.5(i)): A law enforcement officer, as defined in section 710-1000, shall be permitted to search a person convicted under this section, including the person's motor vehicle and the person's residence, for firearms without obtaining a search warrant pursuant to chapter 803 if the law enforcement officer has reason to believe acts of harassment by the person are imminent.
